summary:
**MISSION: ORBIT – Interactive Space Mission Design and Simulation Platform**

MISSION: ORBIT is an educational, game-based space mission design and simulation platform that allows users to explore the Solar System and experience the process of planning and managing space missions. Users can select destinations such as the Moon, Mars, and asteroids, define scientific objectives, design spacecraft by selecting different components, and evaluate engineering factors such as mass, power consumption, budget, and launch compatibility.

The platform addresses the challenge of making complex space exploration concepts more accessible and engaging through interactive 3D visualisation, simplified engineering simulations, mission-control experiences, and decision-based mission scenarios. Users can observe how their spacecraft designs and mission decisions influence outcomes while learning about scientific instruments, orbital missions, and space technology.

MISSION: ORBIT is important because it makes space science and engineering more approachable, encourages practical STEM learning, and inspires students to understand the planning, challenges, and innovation behind space exploration.
details:
MISSION: ORBIT – Interactive Space Mission Design and Simulation Platform

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

MISSION: ORBIT is an interactive, game-based educational platform that allows users to experience the planning, design, and execution of space exploration missions. Users can explore destinations such as the Moon, Mars, and asteroids, select scientific objectives, and build their own spacecraft by choosing components such as cameras, scientific instruments, antennas, batteries, solar panels, and propulsion systems.

The platform evaluates spacecraft designs using simplified engineering calculations involving total mass, power consumption, available budget, communication capability, and launch vehicle compatibility. Once the spacecraft is ready, users can proceed through a simulated launch and mission journey, encounter unexpected mission events, make decisions, and observe how their choices affect the mission outcome. At the end, users receive mission results, performance scores, and recommendations.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Practical STEM learning: Helps users understand space science, spacecraft systems, and basic aerospace engineering concepts through interactive experiences.
  • Learning by experimentation: Allows users to modify spacecraft designs and understand the consequences of engineering decisions.
  • Problem-solving skills: Introduces mission challenges that require logical thinking, planning, and decision-making.
  • Accessible education: Presents complex space exploration concepts in a simplified and engaging format.
  • Creative exploration: Encourages users to design different spacecraft and experiment with missions to multiple destinations.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact of MISSION: ORBIT is to make space science and aerospace engineering more accessible, particularly to students and beginners. It aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration, strengthen scientific thinking, and introduce users to the engineering considerations behind real-world space missions.

The platform can serve as an educational tool for schools, colleges, STEM clubs, and individual learners. By combining interactive simulations with game-based learning, it seeks to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space enthusiasts.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software were used?

Frontend and visualisation

  • React – interactive user interface
  • JavaScript – application logic and interactions
  • HTML5 and CSS3 – page structure and styling
  • Three.js – interactive 3D Solar System and spacecraft visualisation

Backend

  • Java 21 – backend programming
  • Spring Boot – REST API development and application services
  • Spring Data JPA – database operations

Database

  • MySQL 8.4 – storing user accounts, missions, spacecraft configurations, mission history, and results

Development tools

  • Visual Studio Code – development environment
  • Git and GitHub – source-code management and version control
  • Maven – Java project and dependency management
  • Postman – API testing

Hardware: A MacBook Air M1 (2020) was used as the development computer. The project is designed as a web application and does not require specialised aerospace hardware.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

MISSION: ORBIT combines the experience of a space exploration game with the learning objectives of an introductory spacecraft engineering simulator. Instead of simply presenting information about planets and spacecraft, it lets users actively participate in mission planning.

Its creative features include:

  • An interactive 3D Solar System exploration experience.
  • A spacecraft laboratory where users assemble and customise their own spacecraft.
  • An engineering dashboard that translates design choices into understandable mass, power, and budget calculations.
  • A simulated launch sequence and mission-control environment.
  • Decision-based mission events that introduce unexpected challenges.
  • Mission reports, achievements, and progress tracking that encourage repeated experimentation.

This combination of visual storytelling, engineering logic, and interactive decision-making makes learning about space exploration more engaging.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The team considered the following factors while designing the project:

  • Scientific relevance: Selecting meaningful destinations and scientific objectives, including surface photography, mineral analysis, atmospheric observation, temperature measurement, water-ice investigation, and terrain mapping.
  • Engineering feasibility: Considering spacecraft mass, power requirements, available budget, communication systems, instruments, and launch vehicle limitations.
  • User accessibility: Keeping the interface beginner-friendly and explaining technical concepts in simple language.
  • Educational value: Ensuring that each activity teaches a useful concept rather than functioning only as a game.
  • Engagement: Using colourful visuals, 3D environments, animations, mission progression, and interactive challenges.
  • Scalability: Designing the application so that additional destinations, spacecraft components, scientific objectives, and mission scenarios can be introduced later.
  • Reliability and usability: Considering data storage, validation, responsive design, and clear feedback when users make mission-planning decisions.

Overall, MISSION: ORBIT aims to transform the way beginners experience space science: from simply learning about space missions to actively designing, planning, and simulating them.
